issues.title: new_click method missing must_use attribute
issues.description: The new_click method returns a TrayIconEvent that represents an important event which should not be ignored. Factory methods that create event objects should be marked with #[must_use] to prevent accidentally creating an event without handling it, which could lead to silent logic errors.
issues.rule_name: Functions Returning Values Should Be Marked with must_use Where Appropriate

issues.title: Inverted mouse button state mapping in tray icon event conversion
issues.description: The From implementation for converting tray_icon::MouseButtonState to MouseButtonState has the Up and Down states inverted. When a mouse button is released (Up) from the underlying tray_icon library, it's incorrectly mapped to Down in the Tauri TrayIconEvent, and vice versa. This will cause all tray icon click handlers to receive the opposite button state than what actually occurred, breaking event handling logic that depends on distinguishing between button press and release events. The new_click factory method added in this PR uses MouseButtonState::default() which is Up, but when real events are converted through this From implementation, the states will be backwards.

issues.title: PatternJavascript struct gated behind isolation feature breaks brownfield pattern
issues.description: The PatternJavascript struct was moved behind a #[cfg(feature = "isolation")] gate, but this struct is used in webview initialization code (manager/webview.rs line 131) for all pattern types including Pattern::Brownfield. When the isolation feature is disabled, the PatternJavascript struct won't be defined, causing a compilation error in webview.rs when it tries to instantiate PatternJavascript for brownfield applications. This change in the derive attribute placement breaks the fundamental pattern system for non-isolation builds, preventing any Tauri application that doesn't use the isolation pattern from compiling.

issues.title: Config schema/source changed without corresponding generated artifacts update
issues.description: This PR modifies `crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs` (a source file explicitly called out by Rule 14 as driving generated artifacts such as schemas). The diff does not include any updates to the corresponding generated outputs (e.g., regenerated JSON schemas / other generated artifacts that depend on this config). Under Rule 14, changes to this file require regenerating and committing the generated files to keep them in sync.
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code

issues.title: v1 config schema/source changed without corresponding generated artifacts update
issues.description: This PR also modifies `crates/tauri-utils/src/config_v1/mod.rs`, which is part of configuration/schema definitions. The diff does not include any regenerated artifacts that would normally need updating when configuration schema-related code changes (as required by Rule 14).
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14395 - chore: fix new clippy warnings (derive default)

structured_output.summary:
The PR is a mechanical clippy cleanup: hand-written `impl Default` blocks are replaced with `#[derive(Default)]` plus `#[default]` on the variant, across tauri-bundler, tauri-cli, tauri-runtime, tauri-utils (v2 and v1 config), and tauri. Most of the mechanical conversions are correct: each `#[default]` variant matches the removed `impl Default` body. The error.rs change folds the two cfg-gated `MissingBundleTypeVar` variants into one with `cfg_attr`, which is a clean equivalent.

Three things in the diff go beyond or break the cleanup. First, `From<tray_icon::MouseButtonState> for MouseButtonState` in tray/mod.rs has its Up and Down arms swapped, so every tray click now reports the opposite button state to JS and Rust listeners. This is a silent behavior regression that the clippy fix does not need and that no test covers. Second, in tauri/src/pattern.rs the `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` that used to gate only the `impl Default` block now ends up on `PatternJavascript`, which is used unconditionally in manager/webview.rs, so builds without the isolation feature will fail to compile. Third, the PR adds an unrelated public API `TrayIconEvent::new_click` that is not part of a lint fix and is not documented as a public addition.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The tray button-state inversion is a silent runtime regression in shipped behavior and must be fixed before merge. The isolation cfg change breaks compilation for a feature combination, and the unrelated `new_click` public API should be dropped or split into its own PR. The remaining derive(Default) conversions are correct.

architecture.overview:
Tauri's tray support is layered as: the `tray_icon` crate emits native tray events, `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs` converts them into the Tauri-facing `TrayIconEvent`/`MouseButton`/`MouseButtonState` types, and the resulting events are delivered to global and per-tray listeners. Configuration and pattern types live in `tauri-utils` (v2 and a frozen v1 copy in `config_v1`), and the isolation pattern rendering lives in `crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs`, which is consumed by `manager/webview.rs` when a webview is created.

This PR does not change any runtime topology. It replaces roughly 20 hand-written `impl Default` blocks with `#[derive(Default)]` plus `#[default]` on the variant, which is a pure refactor for the config and enum types. It also changes the tray `From` conversion (which is a runtime path and is where the bug is) and adds a new `TrayIconEvent::new_click` constructor.
steps: Start at the native boundary: the `tray_icon` crate emits `tray_icon::TrayIconEvent` with `MouseButton` and `MouseButtonState` values.

`crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs` converts those into Tauri types via `From` impls. The PR changes the `MouseButtonState` conversion (lines 33-36), which currently inverts Up and Down, so every downstream listener sees the wrong press state.

Defaults for the enums that now use `#[derive(Default)]` (MouseButton, MouseButtonState, NSISInstallerMode, WindowsUpdateInstallMode, BundleTarget, PatternKind, etc.) are unchanged in value, so config deserialization and CLI behavior are preserved.

`crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs` now places `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` on `PatternJavascript` (lines 78-81). `manager/webview.rs` constructs that struct unconditionally at line 131, so the cfg change makes the build depend on the isolation feature.
The new `TrayIconEvent::new_click` (line 140) is a public constructor added for testing. It is not required by the lint fix and widens the public API surface of `tauri`.

findings.title: Tray MouseButtonState conversion inverts Up and Down
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs`, the `From<tray_icon::MouseButtonState> for MouseButtonState` impl (around lines 33-36) maps `Up` to `Down` and `Down` to `Up`. Restore the one-to-one mapping (`Up => MouseButtonState::Up`, `Down => MouseButtonState::Down`), matching the `MouseButton` conversion right above it. Add a small `#[test]` in the existing `tests` module that converts each `tray_icon::MouseButtonState` variant and asserts the Tauri variant matches, so the inversion can't regress.

findings.title: PatternJavascript is now gated on the isolation feature but used unconditionally
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/pattern.rs`, the `#[cfg(feature = "isolation")]` attribute at line 78 was left behind when the `impl Default for IsolationSide` block was removed, and it now gates `PatternJavascript` (line 81). `crates/tauri/src/manager/webview.rs` uses `PatternJavascript` unconditionally (imported at line 25, constructed at line 131), so the build breaks without the `isolation` feature. Remove the cfg attribute at line 78 so `PatternJavascript` is always compiled. Keep the `isolation` cfg on `IsolationSide` (line 66) and the other items that genuinely need it. Verify by building `tauri` with and without the `isolation` feature.

findings.title: Unrelated public API `TrayIconEvent::new_click` added to a lint-fix PR
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs`, remove the public `TrayIconEvent::new_click` method (around lines 137-155) that this PR adds. It is not part of the clippy `derive(Default)` fix and widens the public API. If a test helper is needed, move it into the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block in the same file as a private function, and do not make it `pub`.

findings.title: Doc comment on MouseButtonState::Up says "pressed"
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/tray/mod.rs` around lines 21-28, the `MouseButtonState` doc comments are swapped: `Up` is documented as "Mouse button pressed" and `Down` as "released". Swap the two doc comments so `Up` is documented as released and `Down` as pressed.

findings.title: derive(Default) conversions preserve the original default values
findings.body:
Each enum that moves from a manual `impl Default` to `#[derive(Default)]` with `#[default]` keeps the same variant as before. Examples: `WindowsUpdateInstallMode::Passive`, `NsisCompression::Lzma`, `NSISInstallerMode::CurrentUser`, `BundleTarget::All`, `PatternKind::Brownfield`, `TitleBarStyle::Visible`, `IsolationSide::Original`, `DeviceEventFilter::Unfocused`. Config deserialization defaults do not change, and the `serde` attributes on these enums are untouched. This is the bulk of the diff and it is done carefully.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs" lines="801-830"}

findings.title: Bundler error variant folded with cfg_attr without changing messages
findings.body:
The two cfg-gated `MissingBundleTypeVar` variants are merged into one with `#[cfg_attr(target_os = "linux", error(...))]` and `#[cfg_attr(not(target_os = "linux"), error(...))]`. Both error messages are copied verbatim, and exactly one `error` attribute is active per target, so the thiserror derive still sees a single variant with the right message. This is a clean way to satisfy the lint without losing the platform-specific text.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs" lines="101-111"}
